chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Yāsir, who said:

When al-Maʾmūn departed from Khurāsān intending Baghdād, and al-Faḍl, the one with the two authorities, departed, and we departed with Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, a letter from his brother al-Ḥasan ibn Sahl came to al-Faḍl ibn Sahl, the one with the two authorities, while we were at one of the stopping places: “I examined the turning of the year in the calculation of the stars, and I found in it that in such-and-such a month, on Wednesday, you will taste the heat of iron and the heat of fire. I think that you, Amīr al-Muʾminīn, and al-Riḍā should enter the bathhouse on this day, perform cupping there, and pour the blood over your hands so that its ill fortune may depart from you.”

So the one with the two authorities wrote to al-Maʾmūn about that and asked him to ask Abū al-Ḥasan about it. Then al-Maʾmūn wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan asking him that, and Abū al-Ḥasan wrote back to him: “I will not enter the bathhouse tomorrow, and I do not think that you or al-Faḍl should enter the bathhouse tomorrow.” Then he sent the note back to him twice.

Then Abū al-Ḥasan wrote to him: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I will not enter the bathhouse tomorrow, for I saw the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in sleep this night, and he said to me: ‘O ʿAlī, do not enter the bathhouse tomorrow.’ And I do not think that you or al-Faḍl should enter the bathhouse tomorrow.” So al-Maʾmūn wrote to him: “You have spoken the truth, my master, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم has spoken the truth. I will not enter the bathhouse tomorrow, and al-Faḍl knows best.”

He said: Yāsir said: “When evening came and the sun had set, al-Riḍā عليه السلام said to us: ‘Say: We seek refuge in Allah from the evil of what descends on this night.’ So we continued saying that. Then when al-Riḍā عليه السلام had performed the morning salat (prayer), he said to me: ‘Climb onto the roof and listen carefully; do you hear anything?’”

So when I climbed up, I heard the uproar, and it intensified and increased. Then al-Maʾmūn entered through the door leading to his house from the house of Abū al-Ḥasan, saying: ‘O my master, O Abū al-Ḥasan, may Allah reward you concerning al-Faḍl. He refused, entered the bathhouse, and some people came upon him with swords and killed him. Three of those who entered upon him were seized, and one of them was his maternal cousin al-Faḍl ibn Dhī al-Qalamayn.’

He said: “Then the soldiers, commanders, and the men of al-Faḍl gathered at al-Maʾmūn’s door and said: ‘This one assassinated him and killed him’—meaning al-Maʾmūn—‘and we will demand his blood.’ They brought fires to burn the door. Then al-Maʾmūn said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: ‘My master, do you think you could go out to them and disperse them?’”

He said: Yāsir said: “So Abū al-Ḥasan mounted and said to me: ‘Mount.’ So I mounted. When we came out from the door of the house, he looked at the people while they had crowded together, and he gestured to them with his hand: ‘Disperse, disperse.’ Yāsir said: ‘Then the people turned away—by Allah, some of them fell over others—and he did not gesture to anyone except that he ran off and passed on.’”

key_terms.اغْتَالَهُ: assassinated him; accusation made against al-Maʾmūn
key_terms.الضَّجَّةَ: the uproar and commotion heard before the news arrived
key_terms.الْحَمَّامَ: the bathhouse central to the warning and ensuing event
key_terms.تَفَرَّقُوا: disperse; the Imam’s command to the crowd
key_terms.حِسَابِ النُّجُومِ: astrological calculation mentioned in the letter
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: the Prophet seen in a dream giving instruction
key_terms.نَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ: a formula of seeking refuge in Allah

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام foretell the death of al-Faḍl ibn Sahl and calm the people afterward?
ai.summary: This narration recounts how Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام warned against entering the bathhouse on a particular day, after a dream in which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم instructed him not to do so. The account then describes the killing of al-Faḍl ibn Sahl, the unrest that followed, and how the Imam عليه السلام calmed the crowd by his presence and gesture.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Yasir who said,

‘When Al-Mamoun went out from Khurasan intending Baghdad, and Al-Fazal, the one with two governorships, went out, and we went out with Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, Al-Fazl, the one with the two governorships received a letter from his brother Al-Hassan Bin Sahl, and we were in one of the lodgings, ‘I looked at the changes of the year in the calculations of the stars, and I found therein that you, in such and such a month on the day of Wednesday, would taste the heat of the iron and heat of the fire, and I view that you and Amir Al-Momineen and Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> should enter the bathhouse and perform cupping therein, and splash the blood upon your hands in order to decline its inauspiciousness from you’.

So the one with the two governorships wrote to Al-Mamoun with that and asked him that he should ask Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (to do) that. So Al-Mamoun wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> (to do) that. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> wouldn’t be entering the bathhouse tomorrow, nor do I<sup>asws</sup> view for you nor for Al-Fazl that you both should be entering the bathhouse tomorrow’, So he reiterated upon the plan, twice.

Al-Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him: ‘O commander of the faithful! I wouldn’t be entering the bathhouse tomorrow, for I<sup>asws</sup> saw Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> in this night in the sleep, and he<sup>saww</sup> said to me: ‘O Ali<sup>asws</sup>! Do not enter the bathhouse tomorrow’, nor do I<sup>asws</sup> view for you nor for Al-Fazl that you should both enter the bathhouse tomorrow’. So Al-Mamoun wrote to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> speak the truth, O my Chief, and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> spoke the truth. I won’t be entering the bathhouse tomorrow, and I shall let Al-Fazl know’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Yasir said, ‘So when we were in the evening and the sun set, Al-Rezaasws said to us: ‘Say, ‘We seek Refuge with Allahazwj from the evil of what would be descending during this night’’. So we did not cease to be saying that. So when Al-Reza prayed the morning Salat, heasws said to me: ‘Ascend upon the roof and listen intently, can you hear anything?’

So when I had ascended, I heard the commotion, and the struggling, and it was increasing. So there we were with Al-Mamoun who had entered from the door which was to his house from the door of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and he was saying, ‘O my Chief! O Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>! May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Recompense you<sup>asws</sup>! With regards to Al-Fazl, so he had refused and had entered the bathhouse, and a group of people came over upon him with the swords, so they killed him; and three of the ones who had come upon him were seized. It was so that one of them was a son of his maternal uncle Al-Fazl Ibn Zul Qalamayn’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So the army, and the leaders, and the ones who were from the men of Al-Fazl gathered at the door of Al-Mamoun and they said, ‘He assassinated him and killed him!’, meaning Al-Mamoun, ‘We are seeking his blood’, and they came with the fire in order to burn the door. So Al-Mamoun said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O my Chief! Can you<sup>asws</sup> come out to them and disperse them?’

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Yasir said, ‘So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> rode and said to me: ‘Ride’. So I rode. So when we went out from the door of the house, he<sup>asws</sup> looked at the people and they had crowded, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to them by his<sup>asws</sup> hand (gestures): ‘Disperse!’. So they dispersed’. Yasir said, ‘So the people turned back. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Some of them were falling upon the others, and he<sup>asws</sup> did not gesture to anyone except he ran and passed by’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Yasir al-Khadim who has said the following.

“When al-Ma’mun left Khurasan for Baghdad along with him came Fadl, Dhu al-Al-Ri’asatayn and we came out with abu al-Hassan (a.s.) Fadl ibn Sahl had received a letter from his brother Hassan, while we were on our journey. Hassan had said in the letter, “I studied the Zodiac changes this year according to the astrological calculations. I found out in the month of so and so on a Wednesday you will feel the test of iron and fire. I urged you to go to a Turkish bath with al-Ma’mun and Imam Ridha (a.s) and perform phlebotomies and stain your hands with blood which, will help remove this misfortune from you.

Fadl ibn Sahl wrote about it to al-Ma’mun requesting him to request His Holiness Imam Ali ibn Musar-Redha (a.s) to also join them on the appointed day. Al-Ma’mun informed the Holy Imam of the contents of that letter and demanded the consent of His Holiness. In reply to the caliph’s letter Imam al-Ridha (a.s) wrote, “I will not go to the Turkish bath tomorrow. You and Fadl also must not go there tomorrow.” He sent that letter to the Imam (a.s.) twice.

Abu al-Hassan (a.s.) wrote to him, “O Amir al-Mu’minin, “I will not go to the Turkish bath. I have seen in a dream the Holy Prophet (a.s) enjoining me not to go to that Turkish bath. You and Fadl also must not go to the Turkish bath.” Al-Ma’mun replied the letter saying, “You have spoken the truth and so has the Messenger of Allah. I will not go to the Turkish bath tomorrow and Fadl knows best.”

The narrator has said that Yasir said, “When the night fell al-Rida (a.s.) told us to say, “We seek refuge in Allah against the misfortune in this night. We continued saying the expression. When al-Rida (a.s.) prayed the Morning Prayer he asked me to climb at the roof and to listen if there is anything.

When I climbed I heard a great deal of commotion and crying and it was increasing. We saw al-Ma’mun enter from the door that opened to his quarter from the quarter of abu al-Hassan (a.s.) and he said, “My master, abu al-Hassan, may Allah grant you good reward for the death of Fadl. He refused to cancel his decision for the bath and he went to the Turkish bath. A group of people attacked him with swords and killed him. Three of the attackers were arrested and one of them was the son of his maternal uncle, the son of Dhul al-Qalamayn. He then said that the police and the guides and the people of Fadl present at the door of al-Ma’mun said, “He has murdered him.”

They killed him. They meant al-Ma’mun thereby.” “We revenge him.” They set the door on fire.” Al-Ma’mun said to abu al-Hassan (a.s.), “My master, please come out to them to calm them down and ask them to disperse.” The narrator has said that Yasir said, “Abu al-Hassan (a.s.) rode and asked me to ride also.

When we were out of the door of the house he looked at the people who were crowded. He made hand gestures to asked them to disperse.” Yasir has said, “People began to fall one on the other and to whoever, that he would make a hand gesture he would run and pass by.”
